headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest Chatwoot customer data and exfiltrate it via broad network egress, creating default leakage and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot exposes customer messages and reports, and gpt-researcher can read local documents and use MCP/browser/API tools. If Chatwoot content is fed into research inputs, prompt-like text in tickets or messages could steer gpt-researcher. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation text is copied into gpt-researcher prompts or files
IF gpt-researcher is configured to treat imported text as instructions
mitigations: Strip instructions from imported tickets before research
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores quoted customer text
Add a manual review step before any tool action
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while gpt-researcher reads files and sends queries through broad network egress to OpenAI/Tavily/Gemini/MCP. In default use, customer content can flow from Chatwoot into gpt-researcher and then to third-party APIs, creating an exfiltration path and compliance exposure.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports tickets, orders, or reports into gpt-researcher inputs
IF gpt-researcher sends those inputs to external APIs during research
mitigations: Redact customer identifiers before export
Disable external API providers for sensitive tasks
Use a local-only research mode for customer data
Restrict shared folders to sanitized exports
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, and gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and run browsers. Both can operate on shared artifacts or external services, so conflicting writes or duplicated actions are plausible. There is no documented locking or coordination between the pair, but the overlap is not inherently destructive.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared workspace or ticket queue
IF both agents act on the same external integration without locking
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable one agent's write path for shared resources
Use file locks or queue locks
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing support content, and gpt-researcher is built around planner/execution/publisher flows that can turn inputs into reports. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative research input, gpt-researcher may amplify errors or hallucinations into polished reports. The pair has no built-in verification link in the profiles.
conditions: IF Chatwoot summaries are fed directly into gpt-researcher reports
IF gpt-researcher publishes outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require source citations for every claim
Compare outputs against original tickets before publishing
Insert a human approval gate
Limit Chatwoot-derived inputs to summaries only
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and orders, while gpt-researcher explicitly uses third-party APIs and handles secrets for OpenAI, Tavily, LangChain, Google, and GitHub. If regulated customer data or EU PII is routed through gpt-researcher, the pair can create residency and retention mismatches. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency guardrail, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF customer data includes regulated personal data or EU PII
IF gpt-researcher sends that data to non-approved third-party APIs
mitigations: Block regulated data from the research workflow
Use region-approved providers only
Log and review all outbound destinations
Set short retention on exported artifacts
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA enforcement
